_comment: The things receipts can't tell you. Edit this by hand; it is the one file that is not generated. It lives in this repo with everything else, and this repo is public — Charlotte's decision on 2026-09-05.

household.notes: Dinners every night, plus five weekday lunches planned as their own light dishes — not dinner leftovers. Breakfast is the same sandwich almost every morning: baguette, Boursin, charcuterie, a sliced cheese and cherry tomatoes. Plan it every day and put its ingredients on the order — it is the meal they eat most and it was missing entirely until 2026-09-06. Charlotte and her partner eat the same thing: one dinner, two portions. Asked and confirmed 2026-09-15 — there is no split to plan around, so nothing here distinguishes between them.

budget.note: Raised from 100 to 150 on 2026-09-04 to cover 7 dinners plus 5 planned lunches. The separate pantry-week allowance is retired — both numbers are 150 now. Observed average across 23 orders is 86,03 €, but those weeks had no planned lunches. Ceiling, not a target.

dietary.excludedReason: IBS. No heat at all — this is a constraint, not a preference. Aromatics carry the flavour instead: gingembre, ail, oignon vert, sésame, soja, vinaigre, miso.
dietary.limitedReason: Mildly lactose intolerant. Cheese is fine. Coconut milk is not dairy and is unrestricted.
dietary.dislikedNote: Olives came out of the puttanesca and the roast chicken on 2026-09-14 because Charlotte does not like them — recorded then in the recipes on her page, and here on 2026-09-15. Prawns went the same day: she said she does not like shrimp much, which retired gambas-ail-persil. Méré sold no raw peeled gambas anyway.
dietary.boredOfNote: Said on 2026-09-15. Chipolatas are in 17 of 23 orders and were carrying a dinner of their own; move them to occasional and let pork chops, lardons and pancetta take the pork side. Asked about the other heavy repeats — the baguette in 18 orders, Barilla pesto rosso in 11, the morning sandwich seven times a week — she said to keep them: the repeats are the point. Don't 'fix' them.

fish.note: Asked on 2026-09-15 why fish is three purchases in 23 orders. It is price, not taste: the same weight of chicken costs a quarter as much. They do like fresh fish. She asked for the planning rules to be left alone — no fish quota, no cost-per-serving display — so this is here as a fact about them, not a rule. Méré lists no fresh trout fillet (catalogue, 2026-09-14), and fresh salmon has never been looked up; truite-amandes-poireaux is the salmon version now and ships as a guess until it is.

cuisines.notes: Indian means mild curry, never hot. Spring rolls are made often and are a favourite. Half the dinners Asian, half European (French, Italian, Spanish) — Charlotte asked for 50/50 on 2026-09-06, having found the weeks were running about 70% Asian. The library was already half European; it was this field, previously "most", that skewed the plans.
cuisines.fallback: vegetable-forward, and vary it — the European half should not be another gratin every week. Spanish and Italian count towards it as much as French.
cuisines.varietyRule: Don't repeat a dinner within a fortnight while there are unused dishes in the library, and prefer a dish never served over one already served this month.

cooking.batchNote: One base cooked Sunday that seeds two weeknights.
cooking.equipmentNote: Told to Claude on 2026-09-06. The air fryer and the muffin tin were being ignored entirely — use them. Every recipe carries an "equipment" array and the Recipes tab filters on it. A muffin tin is twelve holes; batch breakfasts and mini quiches suit it. No microwave, slow cooker, pressure cooker or barbecue is recorded — don't assume one.

staples._comment: Auto-detected from purchase history, but pin the ones that must never be dropped.

alwaysInclude.name: Ultima croquettes pour chat stérilisé adulte poulet
alwaysInclude.note: Two cats. History shows a single 1,5 kg sac per order, which runs out.

alwaysInclude.name: Canaillou, une marque Intermarché Litière végétale agglomérante à base de bois pour animaux familiers
alwaysInclude.note: Ordered in pairs every time it appears.

alwaysInclude.name: L'Or Espresso capsules intensité 8 — boîte de 50
alwaysInclude.note: 3 pods a day between the two of them. A box of 50 is about 17 days, so this is on every order and struck off when there is still a box in the cupboard.

alwaysInclude.name: L'Or Espresso Décaféiné capsules — boîte de 50
alwaysInclude.note: The decaf half of the 3-a-day. Lasts longer than the strength 8; strike it off most weeks.

staples.coffeeNote: Told to Claude 2026-09-06: L'Or capsules, strength 8, plus decaf, 3 pods a day. The only coffee in the receipts is one box on 2025-10-09 at 17,64 € — and the email truncated the name to "L'Or Capsules de café ...", so the variety was never captured and the exact Intermarché name is unknown. Both lines are therefore guesses at that same price, flagged in the page. Replace them with the exact names off the next receipt that includes coffee, and drop the guess flag.

pantry._comment: Asian staples Méré stocks, from the receipts and re-checked on the site 2026-09-14. These are the receipt names — keys into data/catalogue.json, which holds each one's product page and current pack. They are not search terms.

pantry.goneNote: Found gone on intermarche.com, 2026-09-14. The only rice noodle left is Notre Sélection's flat 3 mm; the only gyoza are three fresh Ginza packs of seven, one of them bœuf ail piment. Kikkoman is still there but only as a 150 ml carafe. Recipes that use these are Charlotte's call — the catalogue carries the alternatives.
pantry.stockFindings: 2026-09-06, from a screenshot of the app: the Légumes aisle returns exactly one leek product, Parole gourmande Blancs de poireaux in a jar at 6,23 €. No fresh poireaux. Two recipes assumed fresh leeks on a guess and were wrong. Confirmed on the site 2026-09-14, along with the rest of the gaps now listed in CLAUDE.md: no fresh parsley, thyme or rosemary, no romaine or rocket, no fresh trout fillets, no manchego. Everything the app can buy is in data/catalogue.json, read off intermarche.com in Charlotte's logged-in Chrome; a screenshot into data/seen-in-app.json is still the route from her phone.

substitutions._comment: Two different things. A recipe adaptation is decided up front and reported. An out-of-stock item at basket time stops and asks.

ingredients._comment: How adventurous to be with products. Set by Charlotte on 2026-09-06.
ingredients.note: Actively use products she has not bought before — pancetta, saffron, anchovies, capers, pine nuts, mushrooms, shallots, arborio rice. These ship as guesses with an estimated price, then get looked up on the site and recorded in data/catalogue.json; once named there, the page lists them under New to you at the real price. Anything already in the receipts should still use its exact name — the key into the pricebook and the catalogue. Dropped from this list on 2026-09-15: manchego and leeks (Méré stocks neither; the recipes that named them use parmesan and the jarred leek whites) and gambas (she does not like shrimp).
ingredients.avoidReason: All carry heat. The IBS rule outranks authenticity — the recipes say where they depart from the original and why.

favourites._comment: Charlotte and her partner star dishes in the page itself, and those live in the shared artifact database under library/favourites — NOT in this repo, and not in the weekly document, so they survive the plan changing. Read them off the page if you need them; nothing here is generated from this file.

flavours._comment: What carries a dish when heat cannot. All four chosen by Charlotte on 2026-09-15 — she picked every option offered, so the rule is simply: anything but heat.

wanted.of: ail, gingembre, oignon vert, soja, sésame, vinaigre de riz
wanted.note: Already the Asian backbone and already in dietary.excludedReason.
Possibly the real house flavour: Maille cornichons repeat through the receipts, alongside mustard-honey and balsamic vinaigrettes.

wanted.of: parmesan, emmental, mozzarella, brebis, Boursin, beurre
wanted.note: Rich without the cream she reacts to. They buy a lot of cheese and no cream — see dietary.limited.

wanted.of: paprika doux, cumin, curry doux, ras el hanout
wanted.note: The gap. Bought exactly once each — paprika doux, ras el hanout, curry tandoori — and never again, so the library never used them. Actively use them now. Warm and aromatic, never hot: the IBS rule is untouched.

proteins._comment: Added 2026-09-15. Every recipe carries exactly one `protein` from this list — the one the dish is built around — and the Recipes tab groups on it. build-week.mjs validates the value and ships the order to the page as config.proteins. The same eight values tag the groups in equivalents.json, which is how parse-invoices.mjs rolls the receipts up the same way.
proteins.charcuterieMeansCured: Cured or deli meat — mortadelle, lardons, pancetta, jambon. Fresh pork, chipolatas included, is `pork`.
proteins.observed: purchase-history.json now carries a byProtein block. Pork is in 22 of 23 orders and beef in 14, while the library gives pork two dinners and charcuterie eight. Chicken is 12 of 23 and has ten dishes. Fish is 2 of 23. Worth correcting in the planning, not in the receipts.

learning._comment: Charlotte asked on 2026-09-15 to be asked more about her tastes. The weekly run stays three questions — the README is right that a longer one gets skipped — so /courses asks one of these as a fourth, rotating question, writes the answer into this file, and moves the question into `answered` with the date.
pending: Peppers are the most-bought vegetable by a distance — green in 14 orders, red in 13, yellow in 7 — with celery, cucumber and broccoli close behind. Which vegetables do you actually want more of, and which are just habit?
Brussels sprouts are 'always welcome' and were never once bought in 23 orders. There is a dish for them now — did it get cooked, and should more follow?
Breakfast is the same sandwich seven mornings a week by design. Is that still right, or do you want two or three rotations?
How far should the mild spice go — a paprika-and-cumin roast, a proper mild curry, ras el hanout in a tagine? Or just seasoning, not a cuisine?
The Asian half is cooked from scratch but the receipts buy it as convenience. On a tired Tuesday, would you rather have a packet of ramen with vegetables than cook?

answered.q: Do you and your partner eat the same way?
answered.a: The same. One dinner, two portions; no split to plan around.

answered.q: Fish is three purchases in 23 orders — taste or something else?
answered.a: Price. They like fresh salmon and trout; shrimp no. Leave the planning rules alone.

answered.q: What should carry the flavour, given no heat?
answered.a: All four axes — aromatic, sharp, rich, and warm mild spice. See `flavours`.

answered.q: Which heavy repeats are you bored of?
answered.a: Chipolatas only. The rest are repeats because they work.

answered.q: Brussels sprouts: always welcome but never bought and never cooked — which half is wrong?
Asian half: cooked from scratch, or more convenience?
answered.a: Scratch is right. Spring rolls were the real gap — added rouleaux-printemps.
